content: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital is a medical institution located in Pakistan. It was originally established in 1921 by Sir Ganga Ram, a civil engineer serving under the British government in Lahore, Pakistan. In 1946, the family of Sir Ganga Ram founded a medical college named Balak Ram Medical College, in honor of one of his sons. Following the partition of India in 1947, the hospital was re-established in New Delhi on April 13, 1954, by Sh. Dharma Vira, a civil servant and a family member of the founder. The foundation stone of the hospital was laid by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India. The hospital is managed by a Board of eminent consultants under the overall guidance of the Trust Society. Fatima Jinnah Medical College, located in Lahore, was established in 1948, just one year after the creation of Pakistan. The urgent need for an institution to train women in the medical profession was strongly recognized at the time. The late Quaid-i-Azam, the founder of Pakistan, gave his blessings and approved the association of his sister, Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, with the institution. The college admitted its first batch of 39 students in October 1948. Since its inception, it has been training women not only from across Pakistan but also from the broader Muslim world and other friendly nations. Graduates of Fatima Jinnah Medical College are serving in Pakistan and internationally. The first principal of the college was Prof. Shujaat Ali, while the current principal is Prof. Muhammad Akbar Chaudhry. The teaching hospital affiliated with the college, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, currently has 550 beds. The hospital is undergoing expansion on an additional 22 kanals of land, which will add 400 more beds. This new facility will be named Fatima Jinnah Hospital. The faculty at the college comprises both male and female educators, all of whom are highly qualified professionals. The college is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities, including modern laboratories, an air-conditioned dissection hall, lecture theatres with audio-visual aids, a pathology museum, clinical academic rooms, a well-stocked library, and an auditorium for seminars and international conferences. The student hostel is located within walking distance of the college and consists of six blocks. Two additional blocks are under construction to accommodate more students. Currently, approximately one thousand students reside in the hostel.
